questions_visited.why_selected: Direct one-mark radian definition mapped to the assigned outcome.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State the centre, arc and equal-length radius condition precisely.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify that the special angle is set by an arc whose length equals the radius.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Giving only an angle unit, or omitting that the angle is at the centre.
lesson_sections_informed: Linking an arc to its angle

questions_visited.why_selected: A second direct radian-definition prompt confirms the recurring one-mark demand.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Give the formal definition without replacing arc length by straight-line distance.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use the relationship between a central angle, a curved arc and the radius.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Confusing the arc with a chord, or saying an arc is equal to the diameter.

questions_visited.why_selected: A third direct definition question supplies a consistent examiner phrasing check.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State the defining geometric condition in one precise sentence.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Relate one radian to one radius-length of arc at the centre.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Giving the full-turn value 2π rad rather than defining one radian.

questions_visited.why_selected: The opened source contains a direct arc-length-over-radius calculation of an angle in radians.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Recognise an arc length and radius, then calculate angular displacement in radians.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Rearrange s = rθ to θ = s/r and retain rad as the angular unit.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using arc length divided by diameter, or reporting metres rather than radians.
lesson_sections_informed: Linking an arc to its angle
Worked example: finding angular displacement from an arc

questions_visited.why_selected: The opened source uses the same arc-length relationship in the reverse direction, showing why the lesson must teach the symbols and rearrangement.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Connect a circular path length and an angle in radians to a radius.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use s = rθ and isolate the required quantity before substitution.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using degrees in s = rθ, or failing to distinguish arc length from radius.
